title: Fixed-term contract: mandatory writing and successive contracts
summary: Have each fixed-term contract signed before work starts. Check contract history before any renewal.
body: Articles 9 to 11 of the July 3, 1978 law require individual written documentation specifying the end date or clearly defined work. Without this writing, indefinite-term employment rules apply, except for sector-specific exceptions. The law was published August 22, 1978.

Uninterrupted succession attributable to the worker is presumed to constitute indefinite employment, unless justified by the nature of work or legitimate cause. Article 10bis allows a maximum of four fixed-term contracts, each at least three months, over two years total. With prior authorization from Labor Law Enforcement, each fixed-term contract must last at least six months and the total cannot exceed three years.

The fixed-term contract expires normally without notice. Work continuation after its end normally triggers indefinite-term employment rules. A succession mixing fixed-term and replacement contracts must also be subject to separate review.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Trial period: abolition in ordinary contracts
summary: Do not insert a trial period in an ordinary contract. Student and temporary work contracts retain special rules.
body: Since January 1, 2014, a trial clause in a new ordinary contract is null. This removal results from the December 26, 2013 law on unified status, particularly its article 71.

For a student, the first three days of actual work constitute the trial, with termination without notice or compensation. A new trial is forbidden for successive student contracts in the same role, per article 127 of the July 3, 1978 law.

In temporary or interim work, the first three effective days normally constitute the trial. Parties may waive it or adapt its duration, which must remain proportionate to the contract and work. Successive trials are forbidden. Basis: article 5 of the July 24, 1987 law.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Dismissal: notice period by seniority in 2026
summary: Choose the notice table according to contract start date and seniority. Two changes apply to new contracts in 2026.
body: For contracts starting from August 1, 2026, the notice period is one week before six months' seniority, six weeks from six to less than nine months, then seven weeks from nine to less than twelve months. The table is the same for manual workers and employees.

For contracts started since January 1, 2014 but before August 1, 2026, initial tranches remain different: one week before three months, three weeks from three to less than four months, four weeks from four to less than five months and five weeks from five to less than six months.

For contracts starting from June 1, 2026, the notice period is capped at 52 weeks from seventeen years' seniority. This cap does not concern earlier contracts. Contracts started before 2014 require distinct transitional rules.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Resignation: notice period duration
summary: Verify the candidate's notice period before setting availability. The first six months rule changes for contracts starting from August 1, 2026.
body: For these new contracts, the worker owes one week notice before six months' seniority. For contracts started earlier, they owe one week before three months and two weeks from three to less than six months.

Thereafter, periods are three weeks from six to less than twelve months, four from twelve to less than eighteen months, five from eighteen to less than twenty-four months and six from two to less than four years.

The table provides seven weeks from four to less than five years, nine from five to less than six years, ten from six to less than seven years and twelve from seven to less than eight years. From eight years, the maximum is thirteen weeks. These periods apply to both manual workers and employees.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Part-time: written contract content
summary: Part-time work requires individual written documentation from work start. Specify the agreed weekly regime and schedule.
body: Article 11bis of the July 3, 1978 law requires writing by work commencement. The contract distinguishes weekly duration, called regime, from work days and times, called schedule. Specifications must be adapted to the fixed or variable character of each.
Absent compliant writing, the worker may choose the most favorable regime and schedule among those applied in the company. This deficiency does not, by itself, create a right to full-time status.

Keep a copy or signed excerpt of the contract where the work rules can be consulted, per publicity rules of the December 22, 1989 law-program. Since June 1, 2026, the general weekly limit is one-tenth of the reference full-time duration, subject to exceptions.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Part-time: minimum reduced to one-tenth in June 2026
summary: The general one-third rule was replaced by one-tenth on June 1, 2026. Adapt recruitment offer and contract templates.
body: The May 18, 2026 law on various work-related provisions, published June 1, 2026, reduces part-time weekly minimum duration from 1/3 to 1/10 of full-time workers. This change appears in articles 5 to 9 and 27.

For a hiring taking effect from June 1, 2026, do not present one-third-time as general legal minimum. Check applicable exceptions; the law maintains the possibility to exempt by royal decree for certain sectors, companies or workers. This reform of weekly volume does not dispense from checking other rules on services and schedules.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Variable part-time: notification and schedule retention
summary: Plan specific framework in work rules and communicate each schedule in advance. Simple mention of 'flexible schedules' is not sufficient.
body: The writing indicates fixed weekly duration or average duration with its reference period, as well as the variable character of the schedule. The rules set possible days, time ranges, minimum and maximum durations and notification procedures.

Notify a written, dated and individual notice at least seven working days in advance. A mandatory collective agreement may shorten this period, in principle to a minimum of three working days; verify sector exceptions noted by SPF.

Keep the notice where the rules are viewable during its application, then for one year. Record deviations from schedules. Bases: article 11bis of the July 3, 1978 law and articles 157, 159 and 160 to 169 of the December 22, 1989 law-program. The general schedule framework allowed since June 2026 does not replace this specific framework.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Part-time: minimum services and monitoring
summary: Verify service duration and ensure schedule traceability. The reduced 2026 weekly minimum does not eliminate the three-hour per-service general rule.
body: Each service lasts normally at least three hours, full-time or part-time. A royal decree or collective agreement may provide an exception. Since June 1, 2026, the part-time weekly minimum is one-tenth of full-time of the same category in the company, or failing that of the sector. Exceptions remain possible. If the contract provides less than authorized minimum, salary remains due on this minimum basis.

Keep the contract or its signed excerpt where work rules can be viewed. Record deviations from announced schedule in a reliable time-tracking system or in the regulatory document. Failure to publicize schedules or record deviations creates a rebuttable presumption of full-time services.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Full-time: 38 hours and compensatory rest
summary: Verify sector duration before announcing full-time. Distinguish actual worked hours from average obtained through compensatory rest.
body: The general framework provides eight hours per day and forty hours per week, subject to exceptions. Since January 1, 2003, reduction to 38 weekly hours applies to affected companies. It may be effective or achieved on average through compensatory rest.

SPF gives the example of forty effective hours with twelve compensatory rest days per year to achieve 38 hours annual average. This number must not be automatically applied to all regimes. Check applicable collective agreement and acquisition rules.

Conventional limits replace legal limits for exceptions, rest and overtime per article 28 of the March 16, 1971 law. Article 19 defines work as time at the employer's disposal. Also verify field exclusions, notably certain management or trust functions.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Work rules: delivery, content, and filing
summary: Prepare applicable work rules before the employee's arrival and provide them a copy. The obligation exists regardless of employer size subject to law.
body: The April 8, 1965 law frames content and procedure. Article 6 notably provides schedules or their authorized framework, salary payment, termination rules, leave and references to applicable collective agreements. Since June 2026, certain schedules may fit a general normal working time framework.
Provide a copy at each start and upon changes; keep proof of delivery. A copy must remain accessible without intermediary at each work location, including temporary worksites.

File the rules with Labor Law Enforcement within eight days of entry into force, possibly online. Without a works council, the draft is posted and workers have fifteen days to submit observations. Respect consultation procedure before modifying conditions announced to the candidate.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: RMMMG: 2,189.81 € since April 2026
summary: The National Labor Council indicates a minimum guaranteed average monthly income of 2,189.81 € since April 1, 2026. First check applicable sector minimum for the position.
body: Collective agreement No. 43 of May 2, 1988 frames minimum guaranteed average monthly income. The increase step of April 1, 2026 is achieved by collective agreement No. 43/18. The amount published by the Council concerns workers aged 18 and over under this regime.

Minimum guaranteed average monthly income does not necessarily correspond only to monthly base salary: certain annual compensation, like a thirteenth month, enters verification. An individual contract cannot fall below the minimum set by the applicable sector collective agreement.

Do not indiscriminately apply this amount to students aged 18 to 20: they fall under the reduced minimum of collective agreement No. 50. Collective agreement No. 43 does not cover ages 16 and 17 or young people in apprenticeship training either. For part-time, check collective agreement No. 35 procedures.

title: Indexation: limitation above 4,000 € in 2026
summary: Check sector indexation mechanism and new moderation before calculating a salary increase. The 'index cents' applies from June 1, 2026.
body: The May 30, 2026 law-program, title 3, chapter 1, limits indexation of the portion of reference salary exceeding 4,000 € gross to application of 2% moderation. Up to and including 4,000 €, indexation remains full. The concrete date depends on the applicable indexation mechanism.

The threshold concerns fixed base monthly gross salary, scale or contractual, reduced to full-time. Overtime, meal vouchers, performance or year-end bonuses, eco-vouchers, profit-sharing bonuses and night or weekend increases are excluded.

Parties cannot waive this limitation by particular agreement. To prepare the offer and budget, identify the indexation collective agreement and have salary verification done by payroll. The source announces a second application from January 1, 2028, a date still subject to postponement.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Interim: authorized reasons and written contract
summary: Justify interim use by legal reason and verify corresponding procedure. The agency remains the legal employer.
body: The July 24, 1987 law and collective agreement No. 108 frame six reasons: replacement, temporary excess, exceptional work, insertion toward permanent hiring, certain artistic services and regional work placement. Maximum duration and required consultations vary by reason.

The contract must be written by work start. Since June 1, 2026, the separate prior intent statement is removed; contract writing remains mandatory. The user must transmit necessary information to the agency.

The user is responsible for applying working time and safety rules on their site. Use outside authorized cases may create indefinite employment between them and the temporary worker. Do not use temporary work as mere trial period without admissible cause.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Non-compete: thresholds and conditions in 2026
summary: Check salary, role and collective agreement before inserting a non-compete clause. Thresholds are assessed at termination.
body: Since January 1, 2026, gross annual compensation must exceed 44,447 €. Up to 88,895 €, a collective agreement must designate affected roles. Beyond 88,895 €, the salary condition allows the clause, except roles excluded by collective agreement; other conditions remain mandatory.

The clause must be written, target similar activities and limited real competition zone in Belgium. Its duration cannot exceed twelve months. Provide compensation of at least half the gross compensation corresponding to this duration, unless the employer waives within fifteen days of termination.

These conditions are cumulative. The ordinary clause notably has no effect upon termination during the first six months or dismissal without grave fault of the worker. Articles 65 and 86 of the July 3, 1978 law frame this regime; certain international clauses and commercial representatives follow particular rules.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Meal vouchers: ONSS conditions and 2026 ceiling
summary: Check collective agreement or individual agreement before promising meal vouchers. Exemption depends on several cumulative conditions.
body: Since January 1, 2026, maximum employer contribution exempt is 8.91 € per voucher; worker contribution is at least 1.09 €. The employer ceiling follows the November 10, 2025 royal decree, published November 17, 2025.

Provision must rest on a sector or company collective agreement. Individual written agreement is admitted only in provided situations, notably absent union delegation. Also check sector collective agreement limits. Substitution for existing compensation is principally excluded; eco-voucher replacement benefits an exception.

The principle is one voucher per day actually worked, including part-time, subject to alternative counting allowed. Vouchers are electronic and valid twelve months. Leave or sick days normally give no voucher entitlement. Detailed conditions appear in ONSS 2026/3 instructions.

title: Eco-vouchers: entitlement, limits and 2026 list
summary: Eco-vouchers are not automatic entitlement for everyone. Verify applicable collective agreement or authorized individual agreement.
body: Collective agreement No. 98 sets the private sector minimal framework and permitted purchases. The exemption notably requires maximum 10 € per voucher value and 250 € maximum per worker per year. Validity period is twenty-four months.

The sector or company collective agreement specifies amount and procedures. Individual agreement is possible in authorized cases, notably absent union delegation. For mid-year start or end, calculation must at least account for contract period and provided assimilations.

The list of permitted purchases was amended by collective agreement No. 98/12 of February 24, 2026, effective June 1, 2026. Use this list to describe the benefit. Social conditions notably fall under article 19quater of the November 28, 1969 royal decree.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Regular telework: written agreement and expenses
summary: Structured telework is voluntary and must be formalized individually. Collective Agreement No. 85 governs conditions to announce and contractualize.
body: Articles 2 and 5 target regular work outside facilities, via information technology, which could be performed in the company. The regime does not cover mere mobile work. Telework may be agreed at hiring or later.

Article 6 imposes writing by telework start, or an amendment to existing contract. Mention its frequency, availabilities and contact means, technical support, expenses, return procedures and chosen places. Absent writing, the worker may enter or re-enter facilities.

Articles 7 to 10 guarantee comparable conditions and require the employer provide equipment, its maintenance and connection and communication costs. If the employee uses their own equipment, set expense coverage for telework-related costs before start. The coordinated version integrates collective agreement No. 85 bis, effective February 27, 2008.
